items.title: [Bugfix][MooncakeStore] Fix finish-time save crash on hybrid models
items.body:
## What & why

Fixes a crash in `MooncakeStoreConnector`'s save path on hybrid (multi KV-group) models such as Kimi-K3 (MLA + GDN):

```
worker.py: KVCacheStoreSendingThread → _handle_request
  group_blocks = block_ids_per_group[g_idx]
IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

## Root cause

Under `MultiConnector`, `update_state_after_alloc` forwards the real `num_external_tokens` only to the connector that supplied them; every other connector is called with `0` (`multi_connector.py`). The store connector used that as a condition to record an **empty** block-table tuple in `_unfinished_requests`:

```python
local_block_ids: tuple[list[int], ...] = ()
if num_external_tokens > 0:   # never true for the non-chosen connector
    local_block_ids = ...
```

The finish-time save path (`scheduler.py`, requests that left the schedule with a load spec) rebuilds the request tracker from that stored entry, so the worker's per-group save loop indexed into an empty tuple — on hybrid models with N>1 KV groups this raises `IndexError` per affected request. Each crash silently drops that request's store save (store pool stays under-populated); single-group models never hit it.

Observed live on Kimi-K3 PD + store offload (GB300): 997 crashes in one eval run while ~7 GB of saves still succeeded via the in-schedule path.

## Fix

- `store/scheduler.py::update_state_after_alloc`: always record the full-width per-group block table (drop the `num_external_tokens > 0` condition). The stored tuple's only consumer is the finish-time save, which needs it regardless of who supplied external tokens.
- `store/worker.py::_handle_request`: skip (with a warning) any group the request metadata does not cover, so a malformed entry can never kill the sending thread again.

## Tests

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -q
# 183 passed (GB300, aarch64, CUDA 13.3), incl. new regression test
# test_update_state_records_blocks_without_external_tokens
```

Live-verified on Kimi-K3 1P1D (TP8) + `MultiConnector(NixlConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector)` with a deliberately tiny GPU KV pool (`--num-gpu-blocks-override 24`) to force store read/write traffic: gsm8k accuracy holds at 0.967 (0 request errors) and the IndexError is gone.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); a human reviewed the diff and ran the tests above.

items.title: [Bugfix] Include multimodal limits in the model compile-cache hash
items.body:
## Purpose

`ModelConfig.compute_hash()` feeds the torch.compile / AOT compilation cache key. It already
accounts for `language_model_only`, with this note:

```python
# NOTE: For some models (e.g, Qwen3-VL), whether the MM code path is enabled
# affects the computation graph of the language model, therefore we add it
# here early.
if self.multimodal_config:
    factors["language_model_only"] = self.multimodal_config.language_model_only
```

But `language_model_only` is not the only switch that disables the MM code path.
`MultiModalRegistry.supports_multimodal_inputs()` also falls back to text-only mode when **every
supported modality is limited to 0**, unless `enable_mm_embeds` is set:

```python
if all(mm_config.get_limit_per_prompt(modality) == 0
       for modality in info.supported_mm_limits):
    if mm_config.enable_mm_embeds:
        return True
    logger.info_once("All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model "
                     "are set to 0, running in text-only mode.")
    return False
```

Neither `limit_per_prompt` nor `enable_mm_embeds` takes part in the hash — in fact
`limit_mm_per_prompt` is listed in `ignored_factors`. That matters because the two modes call the
model with *different arguments*: `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run()` passes `inputs_embeds` (with
`input_ids=None`) on the multimodal path, and `input_ids` (with `inputs_embeds=None`) in text-only
mode. Those are structurally different graphs, so they must not share a compile-cache entry.

## The bug

Serving a multimodal checkpoint once normally, then again with all modality limits set to 0,
makes vLLM load the **cached artifact traced for the multimodal path** and run it against
`inputs_embeds=None`:

```
$ vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4 \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}'
...
INFO [registry.py:141] All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0,
                       running in text-only mode.
INFO [decorators.py:311] Directly load AOT compilation from path
     .../torch_aot_compile/792be8ffa70c56aa802cd4568487262f5962347a6d51f3c3aab392ddcef4c244/rank_0_0/model
ERROR [core.py:1346]   File ".../models/gemma4_mm.py", line 2088, in forward
ERROR [core.py:1346]     hidden_states = self.language_model.model(
ERROR [core.py:1346]   File ".../models/gemma4.py", line 1269, in forward
ERROR [core.py:1346]   File ".../torch/_dynamo/utils.py", line 5543, in call_size
ERROR [core.py:1346]     return x.size(i)
ERROR [core.py:1346] AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

The cache directory hash is byte-identical between the two runs, which is the smoking gun.
Reproduced directly:

```python
M = "nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4"
ModelConfig(M).compute_hash()
# a2da7650cdca3ecfcedaf8214c807950cc89a9abdbf9dad650d171aa532dfc16
ModelConfig(M, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 0, "audio": 0}).compute_hash()
# a2da7650cdca3ecfcedaf8214c807950cc89a9abdbf9dad650d171aa532dfc16   <-- same
```

This is not specific to Gemma-4; any multimodal model whose LM forward is compiled with the
`inputs_embeds` path can hit it.

## Fix

Extend the existing `if self.multimodal_config:` block with the two remaining switches that decide
whether the MM code path runs. Only the per-modality `count` is hashed — the other dummy-data
options (e.g. image width/height) only shape profiling inputs, not the graph — and `count` is also
what keeps the factors JSON-serializable, since `hash_factors()` uses `json.dumps` while
`limit_per_prompt` values are `BaseDummyOptions` dataclasses.

After the fix the two hashes diverge and the server starts correctly in text-only mode.

## Test Plan

- New regression tests in `tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py`:
  - `test_zero_mm_limits_affect_model_hash`
  - `test_enable_mm_embeds_affects_model_hash`
- The existing `test_language_model_only_does_not_affect_mm_hash` still passes: this change is in
  `ModelConfig.compute_hash()`, not `MultiModalConfig.compute_hash()`, so the ViT-scoped hash is
  deliberately left alone.
- Repro is on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120) with `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` on v0.28.0:
  serving once with multimodal enabled and then again with
  `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}'` under otherwise-identical flags
  reproduces the crash, and the two runs are logged loading the same
  `torch_aot_compile/<hash>` directory.
- With the patch applied to the same install, the two configurations produce different hashes
  (`3b03dbfc...` vs `5aff68fe...`), so the text-only start no longer resolves to the multimodal
  artifact and compiles its own.
- Note for reviewers reproducing this: the cache entry must first be **primed by a multimodal
  run under identical flags**. Starting straight into text-only mode on a machine with no prior
  cache entry compiles fresh and succeeds, hiding the bug.
- I have not been able to run the post-fix end-to-end serve on that box (it became unreachable);
  happy to add that result, and I would welcome a check on a second multimodal model.

## Note on cache invalidation

This changes the compile-cache key for multimodal models, so the first start after upgrading
recompiles once. Text-only models are unaffected (the block is guarded by `if self.multimodal_config`).

items.title: [Bugfix] Add worker-side watchdog for wedged device kernels
items.body:
The FlashMLA sparse-decode MLA kernel can wedge silently: ptxas lowers `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` into CTA-pair TMEM-allocation spin loops with no timeout, so a stalled rank spins at 100% SM utilization while the only error surfaces 300s later in an unrelated collective. The loops are ptxas-generated and cannot be bounded at source level, so this PR arms a worker-side watchdog around `execute_model` (reusing `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) that logs a rank-local diagnostic, and compiles FlashMLA with `-lineinfo` so cuda-gdb captures map to source.

Closes #51035

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement SupportsPP on more MTP drafters (Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, GLM4-MoE)
items.body:
## Summary

Extends the SupportsPP treatment from #46994 (DeepSeek + Qwen3.5) and #53408 (DSv4) to five more MTP draft classes. Without it, running any of these models under `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` with `--speculative-config method:mtp` fails in `create_engine_config` with:

```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.
```

## Files

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mtp.py` (`KimiK3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mtp.py` (`KimiK3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/mtp.py` (`MiniMaxM3MTP`)
- `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/mtp.py` (`MiniMaxM3MTP`)
- `vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_mtp.py` (`Glm4MoeMTP`)

Same mechanical fix per class:
1. `SupportsPP` mixin on the outer MTP class.
2. `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(["hidden_states", "residual"], self.config.hidden_size)` wired in `__init__`.
3. `# type: ignore[override]` on `forward` because MTP drafts take an extra positional `hidden_states` (Liskov violation vs the `SupportsPP` protocol).

The drafter is only ever built on the last PP stage (`is_last_pp_rank` guard in `model_runner.py`), so the SupportsPP-shaped `forward` is never called; the mixin and factory only satisfy the config verification path that copies `pipeline_parallel_size` from the target into `draft_parallel_config`. Same rationale as #46994 point (1).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for each target file and for `MTP SupportsPP`. Only #46994 (DeepSeek + Qwen3.5) and #53408 (DSv4) are in flight; both cover disjoint files.

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <the five files>` — passed (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.)

Mechanical, per-class mixin add; no behavior change on the actual per-request path (draft forward call site is untouched).

## Remaining MTP classes

Same audit turned up ~15 more MTP variants still missing SupportsPP (`ernie_mtp`, `exaone*_mtp`, `gemma4_mtp`, `hy_v3_mtp` / `hy_v4/nvidia`, `longcat_flash_mtp`, `mimo_mtp`, `mimo_v2_mtp`, `openpangu_mtp`, `step3p5_mtp`, `deepseek_v32/{amd,nvidia}`, `dots3_note/nvidia`, `inkling/{amd,nvidia}`). Happy to send a follow-up covering those if this shape is agreeable; kept the current batch to five popular families for a small first review.

AI assistance was used for code search and drafting; every line was reviewed by the submitter.

items.title: [Bugfix][MiniCPM-V] Route video_embeds to the shared vision parser
items.body:
## Purpose

MiniCPM-V routes video inputs through the image vision parser, stripping the `video_`
prefix off its multi-modal kwargs on the way:

```python
self._parse_and_validate_vision_input(
    "videos", **{k.removeprefix("video_"): v for k, v in kwargs.items()}
)
```

That works for `video_pixel_values` and `video_tgt_sizes`. It does not work for
`video_embeds`, because the image field is named `image_embeds`, not `embeds`. The
parser pops `image_embeds`, never sees the renamed key, and behaves as if no video
were passed.

`video_embeds` is a declared multi-modal field on both models, in
`_minicpmv_field_config` and `_minicpmv4_6_field_config`. It can be passed offline
through `multi_modal_data`, and #54242 added the chat frontend path for
`video_embeds` content parts, both under `--enable-mm-embeds`. Users hit this in
two ways. On 2.6 the parser returns `None`, which is stored as
`modalities["videos"]` and then subscripted by `_process_vision_input`, raising
`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. On 4.6 the guard reads
`video_kwargs.get("image_embeds")`, which is absent after the rename, so the video
branch is skipped and the video is dropped with no error at all.

Other VLMs give video its own `_parse_and_validate_video_input` that pops
`video_embeds` by name, Qwen2.5-VL and GLM-4.1V among them. MiniCPM-V shares the
image parser on purpose, since its videos run the same vision pipeline, so this
keeps that structure and replaces the prefix strip with an explicit video-to-image
kwarg mapping used by both models.

Restricting the mapping to video keys also stops image kwargs reaching the video
parser. The old comprehension rewrote every kwarg, so an `image_embeds` sent in the
same request was passed through to the video call untouched.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR or issue covers this. Searched open and closed PRs for `minicpm`,
`minicpm video embeds` and `video_embeds`, and issues for `minicpm video_embeds`.
The nearest open PR, #43760, moves resampler tensors between devices and does not
touch input routing.

InternVL looks related, since its `_parse_and_validate_video_input` also pops
`image_embeds`, but it is left out here: `video_embeds` is not in its
`_get_video_fields_config`, so supporting it is a feature rather than a fix.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_minicpmv_video_embeds.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/minicpmv.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/minicpmv4_6.py \
    tests/model_executor/test_minicpmv_video_embeds.py
```

The tests need no GPU and no model weights.

## Test Result

```
3 passed, 14 warnings in 0.30s
```

Reverting both files fails all three tests. Reverting only `minicpmv4_6.py` fails
`test_video_embeds_are_embedded_by_4_6` and passes the other two, so neither file is
carrying the other's coverage.

pre-commit is clean, including `mypy-3.12` run at the manual stage CI uses.

items.title: [Bugfix][Security] Bound embedding densification before to_dense()
items.body:
## Purpose

Client-supplied embedding payloads are deserialized and then immediately densified:

```python
with check_sparse_tensor_invariants_threadsafe():
    tensor = torch.load(buffer, weights_only=True)
    return tensor.to_dense()          # <-- unbounded
```

`weights_only=True` blocks arbitrary code execution, and
`check_sparse_tensor_invariants()` rejects indices that fall outside the declared
shape. Neither bounds the *declared shape itself*.

A sparse COO tensor holding **one** in-bounds non-zero element with a declared
shape of `(2**20, 2**20)` is a completely valid tensor. It passes the invariant
checks, serializes to about 1.5 KB, and `to_dense()` then asks the allocator for
4 TiB. Smaller shapes are worse in practice: an attacker can pick a shape that
sits just under the host's memory, so the allocation succeeds and the page-fill
during densification gets the API server OOM-killed rather than raising a
catchable `MemoryError`.

Measured amplification on a plain checkout (`torch.save` of a
`(20000, 20000)` sparse tensor with 1 stored element):

```
serialized payload size = 1560 bytes
RSS before to_dense()   = 337 MB
RSS after  to_dense()   = 1866 MB      # +1.49 GiB from a 1.5 KB payload
```

The existing `ndim` validation in `ImageEmbeddingItems` / `AudioEmbeddingItems`
cannot help here, because it runs *after* `to_dense()` — the memory is already
allocated by the time the shape is looked at. The same is true of the
`hidden_size` / `dim()` checks in `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, which are all
sequenced after the `to_dense()` call.

Reachable from:

| Entry point | Requires | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` content part `{"type": "image_embeds", ...}` | `--enable-mm-embeds` | `parse_image_embeds` → `MediaConnector.fetch_image_embedding` → `ImageEmbeddingMediaIO.load_base64` |
| same, `audio_embeds` / `video_embeds` | `--enable-mm-embeds` | `AudioEmbeddingMediaIO` / `VideoEmbeddingMediaIO` |
| `/v1/completions` with `prompt_embeds` | `--enable-prompt-embeds` | `safe_load_prompt_embeds` |

Both entry points are behind an opt-in server flag, so this is not reachable on a
default server — but on a server that does enable them, any client that can send a
request can trigger it. The dict form of `image_embeds` fans out
(`{k: fetch_image_embedding(v) for ...}`), so one request can carry several such
payloads.

### The fix

Add `safe_to_dense(tensor, *, parameter=...)` in `vllm/utils/sparse_utils.py` and
route all seven `to_dense()` call sites through it. It rejects a payload whose
dense footprint (`numel() * element_size()`) exceeds
`VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` **before** `to_dense()` allocates anything, raising
`VLLMValidationError` so the caller gets a 4xx rather than a dead server.

It also checks that the payload actually deserialized to a `torch.Tensor`.
`safe_load_prompt_embeds` already did this; the three media IO classes did not, so
a non-tensor payload surfaced as an `AttributeError` (500) instead of a 4xx.

On the default: `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` defaults to 2 GiB, which is a guard
rail rather than a tight bound. 2 GiB is what a legitimate 128K-token float32
`prompt_embeds` at `hidden_size=4096` costs, so anything lower would start
rejecting real requests. The point is to turn "unbounded" into "bounded and
configurable"; deployments facing untrusted clients will want to lower it.
Setting it to `0` disables the check, consistent with the other limits in the
same table in `docs/usage/security.md`.

I checked open and closed PRs/issues for overlap (`to_dense`, `prompt_embeds
sparse`, `image_embeds limit`, `sparse_utils`, `safe_load_prompt_embeds`,
decompression-bomb wording) and did not find an existing fix or report for this.
Happy to change the env var name, the default, or fold the check into the
`MediaIO.get_max_bytes()` mechanism instead if that fits better.

## Test Plan

New file `tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py`:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py -v
```

It covers `safe_to_dense` directly and each of the three
`*EmbeddingMediaIO` classes (the objects reached from `/v1/chat/completions`),
via both `load_base64` and `load_file`:

- an oversized-but-valid sparse tensor is rejected, and the error names the
  offending parameter and the env var
- the attack payload really is small (asserted `< 4096` base64 chars), so this is
  amplification and not just a large upload
- dense tensors and small sparse tensors still load unchanged
- a non-tensor payload is rejected as a validation error
- the limit is configurable, exact at the boundary, and disabled by `0`

Existing coverage that must keep passing:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/test_sparse_tensor_validation_unit.py \
       tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py \
       tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
       tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py -v
```

## Test Result

New tests, all passing:

```
$ pytest tests/multimodal/test_embedding_decode_limit.py -q
16 passed, 16 warnings in 6.19s
```

Existing coverage, unchanged:

```
$ pytest tests/multimodal/test_sparse_tensor_validation_unit.py \
         tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py \
         tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py -q
2 failed, 74 passed, 16 warnings in 117.31s
```

The two failures are `test_empty_prompt` and `test_out_of_vocab_token_ids`, which
launch a `RemoteOpenAIServer` subprocess. They fail with
`FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'vllm'` in my local
setup, before any request is sent — not related to this change. Notably
`test_load_prompt_embeds`, which round-trips `strided` / `sparse_coo` /
`sparse_csc` / `sparse_csr` layouts through `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, passes for
every parametrization.

Before/after on the same payload, using a `(30000, 30000)` shape (3.35 GiB dense)
rather than the 4 TiB shape from the tests, so the "before" branch actually
completes instead of just failing the allocation:

```
declared shape        : (30000, 30000)
payload (base64)      : 2612 chars
dense size implied    : 3.35 GiB
peak RSS at start     : 835 MiB
invariant checks      : PASSED (indices are in bounds)
BEFORE -> to_dense()  : allocated (30000, 30000), peak RSS now 4270 MiB
AFTER  -> rejected    : `image_embeds` declares shape (30000, 30000), which would
                        allocate 3600000000 bytes (3433 MiB) once densified,
                        exceeding the 2147483648 byte limit. Set
                        VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES to increase this limit.
peak RSS at end       : 4270 MiB
```

A 2612-character request field costs 3.4 GiB of resident memory before this
change, and is refused with a 4xx after it.

`pre-commit`-relevant checks on the touched files:

```
$ ruff check <touched files>     # All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <touched files>   # 8 files already formatted
```

items.title: [Bugfix] Stream DeepSeek V4 Vision checkpoint weights
items.body:
## Purpose

Stacked on #54566.

The DeepSeek V4 Vision wrapper currently sorts the complete mapped checkpoint so
all `language_model.*` entries are contiguous. This prevents partial
finalization when a streaming loader interleaves language and Vision weights,
but it also retains every checkpoint tensor in host memory before tensor-parallel
sharding.

This change keeps the checkpoint iterator one-pass. It moves DeepSeek V4 fused
MegaMoE/MHC finalization out of `load_weights()` and relies on the existing
model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` hook after the full stream has
been consumed. The Vision wrapper forwards that hook to its language model.

This follows the same deferred-finalization design as #53379 for Kimi K3.

## Duplicate-work review

I searched the open DeepSeek V4 and multimodal loader work before submitting.
#54566 still materializes the full mapped checkpoint with `sorted(...)`, and no
other open PR replaces that Vision wrapper path with one-pass loading. #53379 is
design precedent for deferred finalization, not a competing DeepSeek change.

## Test Plan

- Add a CPU regression using an interleaved
  `language_model / vision / language_model` stream.
- Assert the first tensor is loaded before the generator advances, protecting
  against full-checkpoint materialization.
- Assert MegaMoE and MHC finalization run only after all weights are loaded and
  see both language-model tensors.
- Run Ruff lint/format checks, Python bytecode compilation, and `git diff --check`.

## Test Result

```text
All checks passed!
3 files already formatted
```

Python bytecode compilation and `git diff --check` also pass. The focused pytest
case was not run locally because this source checkout does not have a PyTorch
vLLM test environment; CI remains required. The originating full-checkpoint
retention failure was reproduced on a two-node DGX Spark deployment, where the
equivalent one-pass loading strategy completed model construction and served a
real multimodal request.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. The commit includes
the corresponding `Co-authored-by` trailer.

items.title: [Bugfix] Load checkpoint KV-cache scales in the Qwen3.5 family
items.body:
### Purpose

Fixes #54623 — the Qwen3.5 family never loads checkpoint KV-cache scales: `Qwen3_5Model.load_weights` hands the iterable straight to `AutoWeightsLoader`, which performs no scale-name remapping, so a checkpoint's `...self_attn.{k,v}_scale` tensors never reach the runtime parameters at `...self_attn.attn.{k,v}_scale`. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` then silently runs at scale 1.0 — including for `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (2.4M downloads), which ships 32 calibrated scale pairs.

This routes scale-suffixed names through `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` before the loader, mirroring the existing pattern in `gemma4.py` / `gpt_oss.py`. Its default pattern (`\.([qkv])_scale$` → `.attn.\1_scale`) already handles this naming; no new remap rules are needed. No behavior change for checkpoints without scales (the suffix gate never fires).

### Test Plan

Hardware in #54623: RTX 5090 (SM_120), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FLASHINFER, MTP k=3 (v0.27.1 image; the gap verified present on main by inspection).

1. Boot with a checkpoint carrying `k_scale`/`v_scale` tensors, `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`.
2. Verify `Loaded weight layers.N.self_attn.attn.k_scale` for every full-attention layer (32 lines for this model). Note: with MTP enabled, the draft layer's scale-1.0 `warning_once` still fires legitimately — see #54623 for the diagnosis trap.
3. GSM8K greedy comparison (n=300/arm, identical flags/seed).

### Test Result

Equivalent change validated end-to-end on v0.27.1 (scale tensors pre-renamed in the checkpoint to simulate this remap): all 32 scales load, GSM8K moves 92.3% → 93.7% (bf16-KV control: 94.5%, pooled n=600). Calibrated values for this model are ~1.06–1.63, i.e. K/V amax exceeds e4m3 range at scale 1.0, so the stock behavior clips.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Restore the chat template content format mismatch warning
items.body:
## Purpose

`resolve_chat_template_content_format` returns an explicitly specified
`--chat-template-content-format` without ever comparing it against the format
detected from the template. The warning that was written to catch exactly that
mismatch has been unreachable since #19735.

## Root cause

#19735 added an early return so that a specified format skips the Jinja AST
parse:

```diff
+    if given_format != "auto":
+        return given_format
...
-    return detected_format if given_format == "auto" else given_format
+    return detected_format
```

Detection also fed `_log_chat_template_content_format`, which has exactly one
caller — below that early return. So the forced path exits before the logger,
and the logger is only ever reached when `given_format == "auto"`. The guard

```python
if given_format != "auto" and given_format != detected_format:
```

is false on every reachable path. `git log -S` puts this at #19735 (June 2025).

## Impact

Forcing a format the template cannot consume fails in one of two ways. Running
vLLM's own detection helpers over the 35 templates in `examples/` (33 usable):

| forced format | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | correct on every template |
| `string` | correct on every template |
| `openai` | 17 raise `TypeError`, 8 silently corrupt, 8 fine |

The 17 concatenate with `+` and raise `can only concatenate str (not "list") to
str`, surfacing as HTTP 500. The other 8 interpolate with `{{ message.content }}`,
so Jinja calls `str()` on the list and renders the Python repr into the prompt:

```
### Instruction:
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Reply with exactly OK.'}]
```

HTTP 200, no exception, nothing in the logs. For those 8 templates
(`alpaca`, `inkbot`, `teleflm`, `llama3.2_pythonic`, `phi4_mini`, `toolace`,
`xlam_llama`, `xlam_qwen`) this warning is the only signal in the system.

## Changes

- Restore detection before the return and select with a ternary, as the code did
  prior to #19735. The override still wins; only the comparison is added back.
- Gate the info line on `auto`, so users who already passed the flag are not told
  they can pass it to override.
- Add `test_resolve_content_format_forced`, covering a genuine mismatch and two
  matching cases.

## Test

```
$ pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py -k forced

[template_chatml.jinja-openai-string-True]              PASSED
[template_chatml.jinja-string-string-False]             PASSED
[tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja-openai-...]     PASSED
```

With the fix reverted and the test kept, the mismatch case fails and the two
negative cases still pass:

```
[template_chatml.jinja-openai-string-True]   FAILED
>       assert warned == expect_warning
E       assert False == True
```

Full file: 62 passed, 3 failed. The 3 (`ultravox`, `Llama-Guard-3-1B`,
`paligemma-3b-mix-224`) are `403 Cannot access gated repo` and reproduce
identically on a clean tree without this change. Built and run from source on
Apple Silicon (CPU backend, Python 3.12). `pre-commit run` passes on both files.

## Notes for reviewers

- **This does not close #54486.** That issue asks for the combination to be
  rejected before request handling; this only restores the diagnostic. Filing it
  as the symptom that surfaced the regression.
- **Performance.** A forced format now runs detection per request again, which is
  what #19735 saved. `_detect_content_format` is `@lru_cache`d and
  `_try_get_processor_chat_template` memoizes through `_PROCESSOR_CHAT_TEMPLATES`,
  so the AST parse and any processor load happen once. The `auto` path — the
  default — already pays this on every request today, so this makes forced-format
  users pay what everyone else already pays. I have not benchmarked
  `tokenizer.get_chat_template()` itself.
- **Eight advisory warnings.** Forcing `string` on a template that also supports
  `openai` renders correctly but still warns, since the formats differ. That
  seems right — you have silently given up multimodal capability — and the
  warning's own text is advisory. Happy to narrow it to the
  `detected == "string"` direction if preferred.
- **Overlap with #53824.** That PR touches the same two files but a different
  function (`_iter_nodes_assign_content_item`, improving detection accuracy).
  Complementary rather than duplicate — it makes detection more correct, this
  makes a wrong override visible — but there may be a textual conflict in the
  test file depending on merge order.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed
line, and the test results above were run locally. The commit carries a
`Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Seed both-XD-RoPE drafting from the xdrope positions buffer
items.body:
Fixes #54555.

## Purpose

The both-XD-RoPE config (target model `uses_xdrope_dim > 0` and draft model `uses_xdrope_dim > 0`) allocates `xdrope_positions` instead of the 1D `positions` buffer, but the draft loop seeds `positions` from `self.positions` for anything that is not `uses_mrope`, so the first both-XD-RoPE drafter with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` raises `AttributeError` on its first speculative step. The seed now reads from `xdrope_positions` for that config, and `_update_positions_dependent_metadata` takes the slot coordinate from dim 0 for both multi-dim flavors: XD-RoPE decode positions are the absolute token index on every dim by construction (`get_rope_state` builds XD-RoPE with `has_delta=False`, so `_prepare_rope_positions_kernel` uses `orig_pos`), which is exactly what the slot math needs.

No model in main implements `get_xdrope_input_positions` yet, so this path cannot be exercised end-to-end today; the fix lands ahead of the first XD-RoPE drafter (HunYuan-VL family per the runner comment) instead of inside it. Non-XD-RoPE paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Test Plan

New `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xdrope_seed_positions.py`: the seed reads the xdrope buffer for the both-XD-RoPE config (and never touches the missing 1D buffer), the M-RoPE and plain paths keep their buffers, `_uses_multidim_positions` covers both flavors and excludes a target-xdrope/non-xdrope-draft mix, and `_update_positions_dependent_metadata` feeds dim 0 to the slot kernel for the both-XD-RoPE config (kernel stubbed, CPU-only).

## Verification

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xdrope_seed_positions.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py -q` -> 8 passed on current main (`810bc32`).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.
- Not run: end-to-end drafting with an XD-RoPE checkpoint (none exists in main yet); the fix is exercised at the proposer state level above.

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3); the crash mechanism was verified by reading the buffer init, the seed path, and the XD-RoPE decode position contract before writing the fix.
